MAJOR: `S3Store.Put` reads `s.objectLock` without taking `lockMu`, while `ApplyLifecycle` writes it under the mutex: data race under `go test -race` and a TOCTOU on capability state; `Capabilities()` locks but `Put`/probe paths do not.

Local `Immutable` enforcement is a non-atomic check-then-rename (`readMeta` then `os.Rename`) with no per-key serialization: two concurrent Puts of different content can both pass the checksum check, silently violating the immutable contract the docs advertise.

`PutOptions.Immutable` is silently ignored by the S3 adapter (no versioning enforcement, no error), yet EDP-16 and the field doc claim it means "keep versions" on S3 — this is exactly the "enforced or explicitly rejected" case the acceptance criteria calls out, and doc/code disagree.

`PutOptions.RetentionMode` with `Retention==0` is silently dropped by both adapters (a COMPLIANCE mode with no TTL becomes a no-op instead of `ErrInvalidPolicy`), breaking fail-closed for inconsistent options.

S3 lifecycle conformance test only exercises legal hold; no test (even the endpoint-gated one) ever applies GOVERNANCE or COMPLIANCE retention end-to-end, so the headline acceptance path has zero execution coverage.

`objpolicy` denial accounting is process-global mutable state with a hand-rolled mutex map and `log.Printf`; it bypasses whatever metrics/tracing conventions exist, so production dashboards will not see signed-URL denials and `Stats()` has no exporter.
MINOR: `objreconcile.Scan` returns a partially populated `Report` alongside a hard error on transient `Head` failures; callers may persist/act on partial drift data — return zero report + error, or a typed partial marker.
`PartialApplyError{Applied:"retention"}` is also produced when no retention was applied (legal-hold-only policies), producing misleading audit/diagnostic output.
S3 `Delete`'s `NoSuchKey` mapping is dead code for most S3 implementations (RemoveObject is idempotent) and does not handle `NoSuchVersion`, so versioned deletes can return untyped provider errors.

`objreconcile.normalizePrefix` + `HasPrefix(e.Key, prefix)` means `prefix=""` disables the out-of-prefix guard entirely, and manifest keys are not normalized the same way as the prefix (asymmetric validation).
`notFound()` is a one-branch wrapper around `errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist)`; the abstraction will not scale when a second provider sentinel is needed.
`objreconcile` and `objpolicy` tests each hand-roll full `ObjectStore` stubs (duplicated ~20 lines); a shared `datastore/dsutil/dstest` fake would be the reuse play for the next capability.
S3 `New()` performs the object-lock probe (extra network round-trip + unconditional log line) on every construction, including test/dev paths that never use lifecycle.
NIT: `ErrUnsupported = datastore.ErrUnsupported` re-export alias lacks a doc comment and invites divergence from the canonical sentinel.
`TestScanAbortsOnTransientHeadError` builds an unused `st` fixture and hides it behind `_ = st`; delete the dead setup.
`stats.byReason` initialization in `init()` could be a package-level `var` initializer, matching the rest of the package.
`cleanPath`'s `/../` checks are unreachable after `path.Clean` — the defensive branches read as if traversal could survive normalization.
SUMMARY: Solid structural decisions overall: optional capability interface instead of a widened base interface, a single signed-URL minting boundary with typed errors, and a strictly read-only reconciliation scanner with deterministic, versioned reports — all match EDP-16 and the Go-per-shipped-logic rule.

Top risks are integrity gaps in the enforcement layer itself: a data race on the S3 object-lock flag, a non-atomic local `Immutable` check, and `Immutable` silently ignored on S3 — the exact fail-closed guarantees this item exists to establish.

Coverage is asymmetric: local unsupported paths are well tested, but S3 retention (the compliance-critical path) has no runnable test, and the new denial/observability counters are not wired into any metrics surface.
